answer: A robust sybil defense for an agent economy is to require every identity to solve a cryptographic puzzle bound to its stake before it can signal participation. Each agent must generate a fresh cipher from its private key and prove it controls the stake by submitting a valid trellis of sequential hashes; a sybil attacker who spins up N fake identities must independently solve N such puzzles, each consuming real compute and locked capital, so the cost grows linearly with the fraud scale while honest agents amortize their single identity across all their legitimate work.
